title: An ACS predicate that runs tests by name passes vacuously when a name matches no test (26 stale names today)
summary: 249 go/acs predicate files shell `go test -run '^(A|B)$'`, which exits 0 when a name matches nothing. At the waves 11-20 review (design doc §5.10, component A1) 26 exact test names referenced by predicates no longer exist, so those acceptance checks pass without verifying anything. go/acs/cycle1678 TestC1678_011 also fails on clean main because it appends stderr after stdout and trims only leading warning lines.
acceptance: A predicate that runs tests by name fails when any exact name matches no test function (verified by name, not by exit code alone).
The 26 stale names found at review are repointed to their renamed tests or the predicate is retired with a reason.
A repo-level check fails CI when a predicate names a test that no longer exists.
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: the acceptance ledger passes vacuously wherever a named test no longer exists, so a regression can ship green; 26 names are stale today
